sentences.en: Last night, my friend and I went to a restaurant and ordered a lot of dishes.
We ate for a long time and were both full, but there was still a lot of food left on the table.
My friend said: "So much food — it'd be too wasteful not to finish it."

grammar.p: 可以 + verb + 吗？ (May I / can we ...?)
grammar.e: 可以 before a verb, with 吗 at the end, politely asks for permission to do something.
grammar.x: 可以打包吗？— Can we get this packed to go?

grammar.p: 把 + object + verb + complement (do something to an object)
grammar.e: 把 moves the object before the verb when you want to stress what happens to it — often followed by a result like 好, 完, or 走.
grammar.x: 服务员把那些菜都打包好。— The waiter packed up all the leftover food.

grammar.e: 太...了 wraps around an adjective to say something is excessively so.
grammar.x: 这么多菜，不吃完太浪费了。— So much food — it'd be too wasteful not to finish it.
